messages:
nora: hi team - quick Q. Our kiddo is covered under both my plan (Redwood Choice PPO) and my ex's employer plan. Hospital says they need the 'primary' insurance card and won't process the other until primary pays. How does coordination of benefits (COB) work here? Do we file with Redwood first or the other way around? Also what docs does Redwood need to reimburse as the secondary?

sara (People Ops): hey nora  sorry for the hassle. Short version: claims should be filed with the primary insurer first (the plan that pays first per the order of benefits). Once the primary pays and issues an EOB, submit that EOB plus the claim to the secondary insurer (Redwood) for possible remaining patient responsibility. If Redwood is primary, we pay first. Order depends on custody, court orders, and "birthday rule" in some cases.

nora: bubble: how do I know which plan is primary? ex has custody alternating weekends, no court order. We're both listed as parents on enrollment.

sara (People Ops): common rule is "birthday rule" for dependent children when no court order: the parent whose birthday (month/day) comes earlier in the calendar year is primary for the child. If there's a court or legal custody document specifying responsibility, that overrides. If unsure, call both insurers' member services and ask them to confirm primary/secondary for that dependent. DM me the two member IDs and I can help call.

benefits-bot: automated note  Typical COB flow: 1) Provider submits claim to primary insurer; 2) Primary insurer adjudicates and issues EOB; 3) Provider or member submits primary EOB + claim to secondary insurer; 4) Secondary insurer adjudicates and may pay remaining balance. Keep copies of all EOBs and itemized bills. Timelines: check plan for claim filing deadlines (often 90 days but varies).

nora: if hospital refuses to bill the non-primary at intake, can I pay now and get reimbursed later? What receipts do I need?

sara (People Ops): yes you can pay and seek reimbursement. Save: itemized bill with CPT/HCPCS codes, proof of payment (credit card receipt), the primary EOB showing amount paid/denied, and member ID info. When submitting to Redwood as secondary, include the primary EOB and the itemized provider invoice. We'll help route it to claims if needed.

billing-rep: provider tip  ask the hospital billing office to bill primary first and then secondary. If they insist on upfront payment, get an itemized statement and note "will submit to secondary" on the invoice. Also get the hospital's billing NPI and address for claims submission.

nora: where do I send secondary claim docs for Redwood? Is there a portal?

sara (People Ops): two options: 1) Have the provider submit the secondary claim directly to Redwood's insurer (we're the group subscriber, but the actual secondary processing is handled by the insurance carrier - check the insurer name on the e-card). 2) If you (member) are submitting, upload primary EOB + itemized bill to the insurer's member portal or email claims as instructed on the e-card. If you need help, send documents to people-ops@redwood.com and we can escalate to the carrier's claims rep.

benefits-bot: automated reminder  When submitting secondary: include both member ID numbers (primary plan and secondary), child's DOB, service dates, provider NPI, CPT/HCPCS codes, itemized charges, and primary EOB. Missing primary EOB is the top cause of secondary denials.

tom: fwiw from the other side - my employer's benefits team said they'll treat the child as primary if my birthday is earlier in the year than nora's. I can DM my member ID if you need it to confirm.

nora: thanks tom. sara  could you paste a short text I can give to hospital billing so they bill the primary first and then Redwood?

sara (People Ops): sure - use this short copy/paste: 

```
Hi [Hospital Billing],

Please submit the claim for [Child Name] (DOB: [MM/DD/YYYY]) to the primary insurer first:
Primary insurer: [Insurer Name] | Member ID: [########] | Policy holder: [Tom Lastname]
After the primary insurer issues an EOB, please submit the primary EOB and the itemized claim to the secondary insurer:
Secondary insurer: Redwood Choice PPO (member: [Nora Lastname], Member ID: [########]).
Provider billing NPI: [#####]. Please include CPT/HCPCS codes and place of service. If you need a copy of the child's primary EOB, contact [Tom or Parent].

Thank you,
Nora
```

nora: perfect, sending now. last Q: if the secondary denies something as not covered, can we appeal?

sara (People Ops): yes appeals possible. Save denial EOB and supporting docs (physician note, medical necessity, prior auth if applicable). Forward denial to people-ops@redwood.com and we can escalate to carrier appeals and help with documentation. If it's a network billing glitch (wrong NPI or missing auth number), sometimes we get it fixed without full appeal.

benefits-bot: final note  Keep timelines in mind: appeals often have strict deadlines (30-180 days depending on type). Submit appeals promptly and include all clinical documentation for best chance of overturn.
